[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a table of camera angles with descriptions, benefits, and cases for each angle.

[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant created a structured table for camera angles including the following details:
- Eye level / 눈높이: Shows the subject at eye level, creating a natural and neutral perspective; benefits include realism and empathy; used in portrait photography and dialogue scenes in film.
- High angle / 고각도: Shows the subject from above, creating a sense of vulnerability; benefits include power dynamics; used in action scenes and establishing shots.
- Low angle / 저각도: Shows the subject from below, creating a sense of power; benefits include emphasizing the subject; used in hero shots and establishing shots.
- Dutch angle / 디트취: Shows the scene at an angle, creating unease; benefits include distortion and imbalance; used in horror movies and action scenes.
- Worm's eye view / 지렁이시점: Shows the subject from a very low angle, creating grandeur; benefits include emphasizing power; used in hero shots and establishing shots.
- Aerial shot / 공중촬영: Shows the scene from a high altitude; benefits include context and scale; used in landscape photography and establishing shots.
- Crane shot / 크레인샷: Shows the scene from a moving crane; benefits include unique perspective; used in action scenes and music videos.
- Steadicam shot / 스테디캠: Shows the scene with a stabilizing rig; benefits include fluidity; used in action scenes and documentaries.
- Handheld shot / 핸드헬드: Shows the scene with a handheld camera; benefits include realism; used in mockumentaries and found footage films.
- Tilt shot / 틸트샷: Shows the scene at a diagonal angle; benefits include distortion; used in horror movies and action scenes.
- Pan shot / 팬샷: Shows the scene with horizontal camera movement; benefits include continuity; used in travel videos and nature documentaries.
- Zoom shot / 줌샷: Shows the scene with a change in focal length; benefits include intimacy; used in music videos and romantic comedies.
